title: Reflection (power, cost, and when it is the wrong tool)
hook: Reflection lets you inspect and invoke types at run time from metadata — powerful for frameworks and plugins, but slow and fragile compared to compile-time code. Prefer source generators when you need metadata-driven code without run-time discovery.

blocks.text: System.Reflection APIs load assemblies, enumerate types, read attributes, and invoke methods by name. typeof(T) and Activator.CreateInstance are common entry points. Dynamic dispatch bypasses compile-time checking — typos become run-time exceptions. Trimming and Native Ahead-of-Time (AOT) compilation require reflection roots or they strip unused code.

entries.plainDefinition: Run-time inspection and invocation of types using assembly metadata.
Creates instances of types when you only know the Type at run time.
Linker removes unused IL; reflection targets may need preservation attributes.

blocks.text: Dependency injection containers, serializers, and ORMs use reflection heavily — you consume it more than you write it. Hand-rolled reflection in hot paths (SQS message dispatch by string name) hurts latency and breaks refactor-rename. Source generators can emit strongly typed dispatch tables at compile time instead.

blocks.title: When reflection is fine
blocks.body: One-time startup scanning — registering endpoints, building DI graphs. Not per-message hot paths.

snippet.label: Discover handlers at startup
snippet.explanation: One-time scan registers all IMessageHandler implementations. Fine at startup; not per SQS message.

snippet.label: Read custom attribute
snippet.explanation: Framework-style attribute discovery. MethodInfo and attributes come from metadata.

snippet.label: Prefer compile-time dispatch
snippet.explanation: Switch or dictionary of delegates avoids per-call GetMethod and Invoke.

snippet.label: DynamicallyAccessedMembers root for trim
snippet.explanation: Annotate reflection entry points so Native AOT and trimming preserve T's methods — or replace with source-generated registration.

blocks.title: Dynamic discovery
rows: Limited; no full type system at runtime in JS

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Reflection inside tight loops. No trim/AOT annotations when publishing Native AOT. Catching TargetInvocationException without inspecting InnerException.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: MethodInfo.Invoke is orders of magnitude slower than direct calls — BenchmarkDotNet on a SQS handler loop shows microseconds vs nanoseconds per dispatch. Reflection is fine once at startup for DI registration; per-message GetMethod breaks under load. Native AOT and trimming remove unreferenced metadata — use DynamicallyAccessedMembers or RequiresUnreferencedCode to document roots. dotnet-trace CPU samples often show System.Reflection.MethodBase.Invoke hot when dispatch is stringly typed.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying reflection is 'free enough' on every SQS message. Ignoring trim — publish succeeds, runtime MissingMethodException on first request. GetMethod without BindingFlags — null at runtime, not compile time. Not unpacking TargetInvocationException.InnerException — hides real fault.

interviewTakeaways: Reflection reads assembly metadata at runtime — flexible for startup registration, too slow for per-message hot paths.
Native AOT and trimming remove unreflected types unless DynamicallyAccessedMembers or RequiresUnreferencedCode roots them.
In production, CPU profiles showing MethodBase.Invoke on request path mean replace with switch, dictionary, or source generator.
60s: Reflection OK at startup. Per-request Invoke is too slow. Generators and typed switches for hot paths. DynamicallyAccessedMembers for trim. Check InnerException on TargetInvocationException.
Follow-up: how would you migrate a stringly typed message router to a source generator?
commonPitfalls: Per-message MethodInfo.Invoke on SQS path gets you rejected — use typed dispatch or generators.
Reflection without trim roots — Native AOT fails at runtime on first use.
Strong answer: 'Startup scan OK. Hot path: switch or generator. DynamicallyAccessedMembers for remaining reflection. Profile Invoke before claiming it is fine.'

jsTsCorrelations.note: import() loads modules dynamically. C# reflection loads types from already-loaded assemblies — different mechanism, similar plugin patterns.
obj[key as keyof T] loses compile-time safety like MethodInfo.Invoke — both break on rename unless codegen provides typed routes.
